definition: Freddy (1969–1971) and Freddy II (1973–1976) were experimental robots built in the Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception (later Department of Artificial Intelligence, now part of the School of Informatics at the University of Edinburgh).
details: Freddy (1969–1971) and Freddy II (1973–1976) were experimental robots built in the Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception (later Department of Artificial Intelligence, now part of the School of Informatics at the University of Edinburgh).

explainer.lead: Freddy II was an experimental robot built at the University of Edinburgh from 1973 to 1976. It followed Freddy, an earlier experimental robot built from 1969 to 1971, and belongs to the university's early work in machine intelligence and perception.

tiers.eli5: Freddy II was a robot made for experiments, a bit like a school science project built to help researchers learn. It came after an earlier robot called Freddy. Freddy II was worked on from 1973 to 1976.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Freddy II as a historical experimental robotics platform, not a modern tool or software library. Its documented setting is the University of Edinburgh, and its 1973–1976 dates distinguish it from the earlier Freddy project.
tiers.paperLevel: Freddy II := experimental robot built during 1973–1976 in the Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception at the University of Edinburgh. Its predecessor was Freddy (1969–1971); the department later became the Department of Artificial Intelligence and is now part of the School of Informatics.

explainer.example: On a research timeline, Freddy occupies 1969–1971, followed by Freddy II in 1973–1976. Both sit within the same Edinburgh department's institutional history, despite its later name changes.

usedIn.detail: Freddy II was built as an experimental robot during 1973–1976.

usedIn.name: University artificial intelligence research

explainer.intuition: Freddy II is best understood as the second dated entry in an experimental robotics effort: Freddy came first, and Freddy II followed. Its identity is tied to the Edinburgh research department that built both robots.
howItWorks: Begin with Freddy, the experimental robot built from 1969 to 1971.
Place Freddy II after it, with a build period from 1973 to 1976.
Locate both projects in the Department of Machine Intelligence and Perception.
Follow that department's later identity as the Department of Artificial Intelligence and then part of Edinburgh's School of Informatics.
explainer.whyItMatters: Freddy II provides a concrete, dated example of experimental robotics within the University of Edinburgh's artificial intelligence research history. The two Freddy projects also show a named sequence of work rather than a single undated robot.
misconceptions: Freddy and Freddy II are not the same build period: Freddy dates to 1969–1971, while Freddy II dates to 1973–1976.
The department's later names do not indicate different universities; they belong to the same Edinburgh institutional lineage.
